text: {"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() decremented s1 (`*s1--`) instead of advancing it, so the first string was read backwards while the second advanced; changed it to `*s1++` to match s2."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strcspn() in lib/string.c iterated with `--p` instead of `++p`, so it walked backwards past the start of the string; changing it to `++p` fixes the strcspn assertion in string_test_strspn, which is the only failing KUnit case."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_get_size(), the loop that reduces a large size by the divisor decremented the unit index (i--) instead of incrementing it (i++), so U64_MAX×4096 produced the wrong unit index and printed \"UNK\" instead of \"ZB\"/\"Zi\"."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "string_escape_mem() read its input with `*src--`, walking backwards through the buffer instead of forwards; changed it to `*src++` so the escape test receives the bytes in order."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_unescape(), a trailing lone backslash was written to dst and then the terminating NUL was also copied (src advanced past it and counted in the return value), so the return length was one too large; adding `break` after writing the backslash stops at the NUL, matching the expected 73-char result."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option(), the negative-number branch used `--cur` instead of `++cur`, so `simple_strtoull` was handed the '-' sign and parsed nothing; this made get_options() stop early on inputs like \"0-1,-3,6\" (test 18), and the fix skips the sign instead."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_options(), the loop broke on any non-1 return code, so a comma (res 2) or a range (res 3) ended parsing early; changing the check to `if (res == 1)` lets parsing continue after ranges and commas, which fixes the \"0-1,-3,6\" case (test 18) and matches the expected outputs for the other range tests when traced by hand."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In memparse(), the 'G' case used `ret << 10;` (a no-op expression) instead of `ret <<= 10;`, so 'G'-suffixed sizes like mem=1G were not scaled, causing the cmdline KUnit tests to fail; changed it to the compound assignment."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In `__siphash_aligned`, the tail length mask was `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)` (i.e. `& 6`), which drops the odd trailing byte whenever len % 8 is odd; changed it to `& (sizeof(u64) - 1)` (`& 7`) to match `__siphash_unaligned`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In the 64-bit `__hsiphash_aligned`, the tail length was computed as `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)` (mask 6), which drops bit 0, so odd lengths like 57, 59, 61, 63 got the wrong tail; changed it to `sizeof(u64) - 1` (mask 7) to match the unaligned variant."}
